title: Choosing Complexity: Cognitive Ability, Overconfidence, and Task Choice
abstract: arXiv:2611.13259v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Workers and organizations routinely choose between complex tasks that differ in their success-payment tradeoff. We study how cognitive ability and overconfidence shape this choice of task complexity, both theoretically and experimentally. Consistent with our model, we find that more cognitively able individuals choose more complex tasks. Conditional on cognitive ability, we find that more overconfident individuals also choose more complex tasks. In about 75% of the decisions, subjects pick their payoff-maximizing task, and higher cognitive ability is weakly associated with more efficient choices of task complexity. But errors are strikingly one-sided: those who fail to choose optimally pick tasks that are too complex. Our findings suggest that organizations should pair task menus and incentives for choosing more complex tasks with information and feedback that help workers assess their ability and probability of success. translated_title: 选择复杂性：认知能力、过度自信与任务选择
translated_abstract: 工作者和组织经常需要在成功概率与报酬权衡各不相同的复杂任务之间做出选择。我们从理论和实验两个层面研究认知能力和过度自信如何塑造这种任务复杂性的选择。与我们的模型一致，我们发现认知能力更强的个体会选择更复杂的任务。在给定认知能力的条件下，我们发现过度自信程度更高的个体同样会选择更复杂的任务。在大约75%的决策中，被试选择了能使自身收益最大化的任务，且更高的认知能力与更有效的任务复杂性选择呈弱相关。但错误呈现出显著的单边性：那些未能做出最优选择的被试倾向于选择过于复杂的任务。我们的研究结果表明，组织在提供任务菜单以及选择更复杂任务的激励的同时，应当配套提供帮助员工评估自身能力和成功概率的信息与反馈。
tldr: 认知能力和过度自信都会促使个体选择更复杂的任务，且选择失误呈单边性——倾向于选择过于复杂的任务，因此组织应将任务激励与帮助员工准确评估自身能力的信息反馈相结合。
en_tdlr: Both higher cognitive ability and overconfidence drive individuals to choose more complex tasks, and errors are strikingly one-sided toward overly complex choices, suggesting organizations should pair incentives for complex tasks with information and feedback that help workers assess their abilities.
